text: Mergo was the infant Great One born from Queen Yharnam's union/contract with the formless Great One Oedon; the birth effectively ended her existence, leaving her a suspended remnant between life and death rather than fully dead.
Mergo appears to have been stillborn or pulled from the womb prematurely, leaving Queen Yharnam chained in blood-soaked white garments in the deepest Chalice Dungeons for countless years.
Queen Yharnam's ancient Pthumerian civilization predates the city of Yharnam by thousands of years.
Queen Yharnam ruled the Pthumerian civilization at its height and was central to its religious practices of blood communion with the Great Ones.
During the night of the hunt, as the blood moon rises, Oedon impregnates Arianna, a woman of Cainhurst vile blood lineage.
The impostor posing as the doctor Iosefka in her clinic also shows signs of being impregnated by Oedon during the night of the hunt.

Ebrietas was discovered and first contacted by Byrgenwerth scholars deep in the ancient Pthumerian Labyrinths beneath Yharnam, using fantasm slugs as organic intermediaries or living antennae of the Great Ones, resulting in a partially successful summoning.
At some point the other Great Ones in the Land of Is departed, but Ebrietas was left behind or chose to stay, and is referred to as the left-behind Great One.

The Choir used knowledge gained from Ebrietas, and her orphanage supplied children as experimental subjects, exposing them to fragments of her cosmic essence in research into guided ascension, believing children's minds to be more malleable.
Most children used in the Choir's ascension experiments died or went mad; those who 'succeeded' became Celestial Emissaries with no memories or identity.
Ebrietas shared her cosmic blood, a purer strain unlike ordinary old blood that does not cause beasthood, with the Healing Church scholars for their most advanced research.
Ebrietas remained alone in the Altar of Despair for years between scholarly visits, long after the Choir's experiments ended.

Rom was once a human scholar at Byrgenwerth who joined the expedition to the Fishing Hamlet, came into contact with the Great One Kos, and was granted insight and cosmic awareness that transformed her into a being neither fully human nor a true Great One, classified as kin.
Rom received her eyes from Kos before the scholars committed their atrocity against Kos and the fishing hamlet, before trust between Kos and humanity was broken.
Rom was placed in the hidden lake by Master Willem to maintain a veil hiding the blood moon's descent and the secret of Queen Yharnam.

After Rom's death, the pregnancies of women touched by Oedon during the night resolve and cosmic, non-human babies are born, previously held back by Rom's veil; a vision of Queen Yharnam then appears in ceremonial, blood-soaked robes with hands crossed over the child she carried, facing a descending moon.
The Ailing Loran Chalice is a key connected to Loran, an ancient city that predated Yharnam and was consumed by the beast scourge in an earlier age.

The Byrgenwerth scholars, including Gehrman, Lady Maria, and church officials, traveled to the Fishing Hamlet, found Kos already dead on the shore, and cut into and dissected her body, extracting and cataloguing her blood and tissue to study her biological connection to the cosmos, in what became known as the Fishing Hamlet massacre.

The parasites that Kos had given to the fishing hamlet villagers were extracted from their bodies and studied by the scholars, who treated surviving villagers' bodies as research resources after the massacre.
Kos was pregnant when she died, and her unborn child, present inside her body during the scholars' desecration, became the entity later encountered as the Orphan of Kos in the Hunter's Nightmare.
Maria was present at the fishing hamlet when scholars arrived and participated in or failed to prevent the killing of villagers and the desecration of Kos.

Gehrman, grieving the loss of Lady Maria, created a doll in her likeness using a fragment of an umbilical cord and a piece of a Great One's biological connection, reaching out into the cosmos and making contact with the Moon Presence.
The Moon Presence bound Gehrman to the Hunter's Dream, giving him companionship with the Doll while taking away his freedom, his ability to age normally, and his chance to die and be released.
The Sword Hunter Badge item description states that Ludwig was the first of many Healing Church hunters, many of whom were clerics, to transform into hideous beasts.
Lawrence, founder of the Healing Church, became the first cleric beast and is fought separately in the Old Hunters DLC.

The Healing Church sealed the poorer district of Old Yharnam and deliberately burned it entirely during an earlier outbreak, killing both the transformed and the untransformed, officially to contain the scourge of beasts; its burnt remains can still be explored.
The burning of Old Yharnam did not stop the plague, which continued spreading through Yharnam via the Church's ongoing blood ministration in other districts.
The player arrives in Yahar'gul after being abducted from the streets of Yharnam by bell-ringing women serving the School of Mensis.
The bodies composing the One Reborn are residents of Yharnam who received blood ministration from the Healing Church and were later abducted by Mensis operatives.
Cainhurst Castle predates the Healing Church, having been the seat of an aristocratic family practicing their own blood arts called the Vile Bloods.
A traitor from Byrgenwerth brought forbidden knowledge to Cainhurst, allowing the Vile Bloods to develop their blood arts.
The Healing Church branded the Vile Bloods as corruptors of sacred blood ministration and sent Logarius to eliminate them at Cainhurst.
Unable to kill the immortal Queen Annalise, Logarius sealed her in the castle's throne room and guarded the seal himself for the remainder of his life.
Ludwig founded the Healing Church Hunters as a formal organization, succeeding Gehrman's original small workshop, establishing ranks and a theological framework for the hunt.
Ludwig eventually succumbed to the old blood and transformed into a beast, merging in equine form possibly with the horse he once rode.
Several hunters throughout Yharnam's history, including Ludwig and Gehrman, eventually succumbed to the very forces they fought against, establishing a recurring pattern of hunting's risks.
Lawrence founded the Healing Church after leaving Byrgenwerth with the old blood, against Master Willem's warnings of overreach.
Lawrence burns in the nightmare because he ordered the burning of Old Yharnam, incinerating a district and its inhabitants.
Byrgenwerth scholars uncovered the buried Pthumerian knowledge about the old blood and Great Ones and ignored its implications.
Blood Ministration, the church's core healing practice, is depicted as having genuinely and effectively treated ordinary illness before its darker consequences emerged.

The deepest layers of the Chalice Dungeon system connect narratively to Pthumeru, an ancient civilization predating Yharnam's recorded history that pursued its own relationship with the Great Ones and developed sophisticated blood-related rituals and technologies distinct from but related to Byrgenwerth's traditions.
The Old Hunters expansion's narrative takes place in the past relative to the base game's main story.
Story revelations in The Old Hunters expansion, especially those about Laurence's uncertain final fate, recontextualize events and locations from the base game.
Real historical fears about contagion and quarantine, including isolating sick community members, echo in Bloodborne's depiction of Old Yharnam's burning and the panic over the beast plague.
Bloodborne's opening sequence has the hunter awaken in Iosefka's Clinic before receiving their first transfusion of old blood.
Community timeline reconstructions attempt to place events like Ludwig's founding of organized hunting and the Choir's escalating cosmic ambitions into a coherent chronological sequence.
